director.chapterArc: A descent from exhaustion into a moment of shared autonomy followed by a grim realization of impending weather.
director.restraintNote: Maintain clinical distance during internal monologue; allow Tonk's dialogue to sound physically strained but not hysterical. The emotional peak is the tethering scene, delivered with quiet competence rather than melodrama.

cues.delivery: Flat and hoarse. Jab's voice is level but the subtext is panic masked by routine.
cues.from: It had moved a long way. The shadow of the leaning rock had gone from his boots to past his shoulder, and the little fire was a grey pad of ash, and his brother was leaning as far out of the hide as the leg would let him with both hands on Jab's forearm, shaking it, and saying his name in a voice that had gone past frightened into something flat and hoarse.
cues.through: "You wouldn't wake up," Tonk said, and then he did not say anything else at all, because he had started crying in the hard shuddering way that took his whole chest, and Jab got him up against his shoulder and held him and looked over the top of his head at the sky.
cues.reason: Tonk waking from a long sleep with Jab unconscious; fear of abandonment.

cues.delivery: Protective and measured. Jab validates Tonk's distress without self-pity.
cues.from: "I know." Jab held the back of his brother's head. His own voice came out perfectly level, which was its own kind of lie and the only one he was prepared to tell. "That was my fault. Not yours. I went to sleep and I shouldn't have, and you did exactly right, and you shouted for as long as it took. That's the job. You did the job."
cues.reason: Jab accepting responsibility for the sleep incident to reassure his brother.

cues.delivery: Voice climbing in pitch. The subtext is the terror of being left alone.
cues.from: "It makes me go away and then things happen and I'm not there." His voice climbed. "And you went away too. And I was calling and you didn't wake up, and if I have the bark I go away and then if you go away there's nobody."
cues.through: Jab sat very still with a cup of bark water in his hand and thirteen days of being the only adult in the world coming down on him all at once.
cues.reason: Tonk articulating his fear that medicine makes him disappear while Jab sleeps.

cues.delivery: Dry and brief. A moment of levity to break the tension.
cues.from: Tonk pulled. Jab's arm jumped and he sat up straight as if something had bitten him, which was partly theatre and mostly not.
cues.reason: The physical test of the tether cord; Jab uses a bit of theatre.

cues.delivery: Quiet and exhausted. The subtext is the cost of survival.
cues.from: At some point past the middle of it Tonk let go of the sleeve and said, in a small flattened voice with nothing in it: "I want it."
cues.through: Jab sat with his wrist tied to a sleeping child and watched the fire.
cues.reason: Jab watching Tonk sleep after a night of pain; realization of their depleted state.

cues.delivery: Measured and observational. The subtext is the discovery of a new power.
cues.from: Then he put his hand flat on his brother's chest, the way he had done every night for six weeks, and let his mind go flat, and asked without caring.
cues.through: "And what do I do," Jab said to the fire, "with a thing that only tells me what's happening."
cues.reason: Jab realizing he can sense the fever's direction but cannot heal it.

cues.delivery: Grounded and sensory. The subtext is the ominous stillness of snow.
cues.from: In the morning the sky had gone the color of a fish's belly and there was no wind at all, and he smelled it as soon as he came out from under the hide.
cues.through: He had grown up in a valley where knowing the difference between a snow that came in on wind and a snow that came down out of a still sky was a thing you learned before you learned to read water. The first kind went sideways and stopped by noon. The second kind sat down on the country and did not get up.
cues.reason: Narrative shift to dawn; Jab recognizing the weather pattern.

pauses.after: The half dose did not hold the morning, and he had known it would not, and knowing had turned out to be no help whatsoever.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the failure of the morning dose.

pauses.after: "You wouldn't wake up," Tonk said, and then he did not say anything else at all, because he had started crying in the hard shuddering way that took his whole chest, and Jab got him up against his shoulder and held him and looked over the top of his head at the sky.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset; Jab's internal realization after Tonk stops crying.

pauses.after: An hour and a half of the best light of the day, gone, on ground where he had planned to make the top of the ridge and get the long descent done in daylight, because a descent in the dark with a frame and a rail was exactly the kind of thing that had put them on a log over a flood three days ago.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on the wasted daylight and danger of descent.

pauses.after: His first thought was that this was the taste, and that he could cover it with the last of the spruce seed mashed up in water. His second was that it was the cup, because the cup had got a crack and a new smell. His third, which arrived on top of the first two and shoved them both out of the way, was that his brother had not said I don't want it. He had said no, which was a different word, and he had said it with his hands braced.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset; Jab's internal analysis of Tonk's refusal.

pauses.after: "That's on my arm all night, every night, from now to the end of the road. You pull it, I'm awake. You don't have to shout and you don't have to reach. You could be half asleep and pull it and I'd be up."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the tether agreement.
Emphasis on the question confirming Jab's concession.

pauses.after: "You're the one it happens to," he said. "It's your night. I'll leave it in the cup and it'll be here."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset; Jab's acceptance of Tonk's autonomy for the night.

pauses.after: Five and a half twists. Two and three-quarter days at the true rate, which was the rate he was actually using and not the rate he had planned.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on medicine consumption rate.

pauses.after: Up, it said. Not the crest and not the fall. Climbing, and still climbing, and higher at the bottom than it had been.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing; Jab's realization of his power's limitations.

pauses.after: "And what do I do," Jab said to the fire, "with a thing that only tells me what's happening."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the nature of his ability.
Emphasis on the ominous weather signifier.
Speaker reset; Jab's final calculation before dawn action.
